expertInsight: Experience Cloud catches most candidates off guard with licensing nuances — the exam specifically tests when to use Partner Community vs. Customer Community Plus vs. Customer Community licenses for different access levels. I counted 6–8 questions on sharing rules vs. sharing sets vs. super user access. Memorize the sharing model comparison table before exam day; it's the single highest-leverage thing you can do in the final week.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Experience Cloud Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: Experience Cloud Consultant is considered one of the harder consultant exams. The content covers niche topics — external user licensing, sharing sets, CMS, and template configuration — that require specific project experience.
bullets: ~65% passing score — moderate threshold, but the content difficulty compensates.
Licensing-heavy — expect 6-8 questions on when to use Partner Community, Customer Community, and Customer Community Plus licenses.
Sharing model for external users — sharing sets, super user access, and sharing groups are heavily tested.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build at least one Experience Cloud site with external users in a Developer Edition org before booking. Memorise the sharing model comparison table.

examFormat.heading: Experience Cloud Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test centre through Webassessor. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 55-65% of questions are scenario-based. Common patterns include selecting the right license type for an external user access requirement, configuring sharing rules for portal users, and choosing the right Experience Cloud template for a business need.
bestWayToPass: Master the licensing model: Know the exact capabilities and limits of each Community license type — this is the single highest-tested topic.
Understand sharing for external users: Sharing sets, sharing groups, and super user access are different from internal sharing and are tested in detail.
Study CMS configuration: Know how to create content, build pages with Lightning components, and configure navigation.
Practice template selection: Understand when to use Customer Service, Partner Central, Help Center, and custom templates.

certificationCard.description: The Experience Cloud Consultant certification validates your expertise in designing and implementing Experience Cloud sites for customers, partners, and employees.

keyConcepts.h2: Experience Cloud Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Site Templates and Their Use Cases
blocks.body: Salesforce provides purpose-built templates: Customer Service for self-service portals with case management and Knowledge, Partner Central for channel partner portals with deal registration and lead distribution, Help Center for knowledge-first sites without case creation, and Build Your Own for maximum flexibility. The exam frequently presents a business requirement and asks which template fits — know the key differentiators of each.

blocks.heading: Sharing Model for External Users
blocks.body: External user record access follows a different model than internal users. Sharing Sets grant access to records matching the user's Account or Contact — without roles or **sharing rules**. External Account Hierarchy allows partner users to see records owned by users below them in the partner account hierarchy. Sharing Rules extend access beyond these mechanisms. Guest users get access only through explicit guest user sharing rules. Know which mechanism to apply for each access scenario.

blocks.heading: User Licensing: Customer, Partner, and Guest Users
blocks.body: Experience Cloud supports multiple external user licence types: Customer Community (limited access, no roles), Customer Community Plus (supports roles and advanced sharing), and Partner Community (full CRM access for channel partners including Leads, Opportunities, and Campaigns). Guest Users have no licence and access via the dedicated Guest User profile. Licence type determines which objects and features are available — the exam tests licence selection for given scenarios.

blocks.heading: Audience Targeting and Personalisation
blocks.body: Audiences define groups of users based on criteria — login status, profile, record field values, or geography. Components and pages can be shown or hidden based on audience membership. This enables a single site to serve multiple user types with different content without building multiple sites. The exam tests how to configure audiences and how visibility rules interact with page-level settings.

blocks.heading: Salesforce CMS and Knowledge for Content
blocks.body: Salesforce Knowledge stores articles for FAQ, troubleshooting, and procedure content — surfaced in search and case creation for deflection. Salesforce CMS is a headless content management system for structured marketing content (banners, news, product pages) delivered across channels. Know when to use Knowledge (support content, case deflection) vs CMS (marketing content, multi-channel delivery) and how each is configured in Experience Cloud.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Experience Cloud Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Experience Cloud Consultant exam tests implementation of portals, communities, and sites for external audiences. Focus on the sharing model for external users, template and component configuration, and authentication options.

blocks.heading: External User Sharing Model
blocks.body: External users have their own **sharing rules** separate from internal users. Know how to configure Sharing Sets (for portal users), External Account Hierarchy, and how Super User Access works for partner users.

blocks.heading: Template & Page Configuration
blocks.body: Know the available templates (Customer Service, Partner Central, Build Your Own), how to configure Lightning pages in Experience Builder, and how to control visibility of components with audience targeting.

blocks.heading: User Authentication Options
blocks.body: Know the difference between username/password login, **SSO** (**SAML**, **OAuth**), social login, and self-registration flows. Understand how to configure login pages, login flows, and identity verification.

blocks.heading: CMS & Content Management
blocks.body: Understand Salesforce CMS for managing content published to Experience Cloud sites. Know the difference between enhanced LWR sites and Aura-based sites and the migration path between them.

blocks.heading: Performance & Moderation
blocks.body: Know how CDN caching improves Experience Cloud performance, how moderation rules and criteria flag inappropriate content, and how to configure contributor roles for community-generated content.

nextCertsAfter.intro: After this consultant certification, you can add adjacent clouds or deepen your specialisation:

sampleQuestions.question: Which Experience Cloud template is best suited for a self-service portal where customers can submit and track cases?
options: Partner Central
Customer Service
Build Your Own
Help Center
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Customer Service template is optimised for self-service portals — it includes pre-built components for case creation, case tracking, Knowledge article search, and community discussion.
whyWrong: Partner Central is designed for partner relationship management, not general customer self-service case tracking.
'Build Your Own' requires custom development, not the purpose-built self-service case template being asked about.
Help Center is more focused on knowledge/FAQ browsing than the case submission/tracking workflow described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Audience Targeting in Experience Cloud?
options: To restrict site access to authenticated users only
To display different content, components, or page variations to different user groups based on defined criteria
To track visitor analytics and report on site engagement
To manage user authentication and single sign-on settings
sampleQuestions.explanation: Audience Targeting lets site builders define audiences (e.g., Gold Partners, UK Customers) based on criteria, then assign specific pages, components, or content variations to each audience — enabling personalised experiences without building multiple sites.
whyWrong: Restricting access to authenticated users is a security/authentication concern, not what Audience Targeting does.
Tracking visitor analytics is a reporting function, not what Audience Targeting does.
Managing authentication/SSO is a security configuration, unrelated to Audience Targeting's content-personalization purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sharing mechanism allows external users to access records associated with their Account or Contact in Experience Cloud?
options: Role Hierarchy
External Account Hierarchy
Sharing Sets
Manual Sharing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing Sets grant external users (Customer Community or Partner Community licence holders) access to records that match their Account or Contact via a defined access mapping — without requiring sharing rules or roles.
whyWrong: Role Hierarchy is an internal Salesforce access structure, not designed for external user access.
Sharing Sets grant access based on criteria matching, not specifically Account/Contact relationship.
Manual Sharing is a one-off mechanism, not the systematic Account/Contact-based access mechanism being asked about.

sampleQuestions.question: What is required to enable case deflection in an Experience Cloud site?
options: Einstein Case Classification
Knowledge Articles surfaced in the site search and case creation flow
Web-to-Case configured in Setup
Email-to-Case with routing rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Case deflection presents Knowledge Articles to users before they submit a case — suggesting solutions that may resolve the issue without agent involvement. Knowledge must be enabled and articles published to the site for deflection to work.
whyWrong: Einstein Case Classification routes cases after creation — it doesn't itself deflect cases from being created.
Web-to-Case captures cases from a public form — it doesn't deflect case creation through self-service.
Email-to-Case with routing is about processing submitted cases, not deflecting them before submission.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature allows partners to register deals and track their pipeline in an Experience Cloud site?
options: Lead Conversion
Partner Relationship Management
Opportunity Management
Deal Registration
sampleQuestions.explanation: Deal Registration allows channel partners to claim credit for potential deals by registering them through the partner portal. It prevents channel conflict and ensures partners receive appropriate credit when a deal closes.
whyWrong: Lead Conversion is a Sales Cloud process, unrelated to partner deal tracking.
Opportunity Management alone is a general sales feature, not the partner-specific deal registration capability being asked about.
'Deal Registration' is the correct answer — Partner Relationship Management is the broader category, not the specific feature name being tested here.

sampleQuestions.question: Which types of users can access an Experience Cloud site?
options: Only Salesforce internal users with a full Salesforce licence
External users (customers, partners) with Community or Partner licences, and unauthenticated guest users without a login
Only authenticated users — guest access is not supported in Experience Cloud
Only users with the System Administrator profile
sampleQuestions.explanation: Experience Cloud supports three user types: internal Salesforce users, external authenticated users (with Customer Community, Customer Community Plus, or Partner Community licences), and guest users who access the site without logging in. Each has different object and record access capabilities.
whyWrong: Restricting to internal full-license users is the opposite of Experience Cloud's purpose, which includes external users.
'Only authenticated users' contradicts the fact that guest (unauthenticated) access is explicitly supported.
Restricting to System Administrator profile contradicts the fact that a broad range of external user types can access sites.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the role of the Branding Editor in Experience Cloud?
options: A code editor for writing custom CSS and JavaScript for site pages
A declarative tool that allows site administrators to configure colours, fonts, and logos without writing code
An analytics panel that shows visitor demographics and engagement metrics
A tool for managing brand assets uploaded to Salesforce Files
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Branding Editor within Experience Builder allows non-technical admins to apply a consistent brand by setting primary colours, background colours, text fonts, and button styles — all via point-and-click configuration.
whyWrong: The Branding Editor is specifically a no-code declarative tool — it isn't a code editor.
The Branding Editor controls visual branding — it isn't an analytics panel.
The Branding Editor is for visual configuration — it isn't a file/asset management tool.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Experience Cloud feature allows an organisation to manage and publish structured content across multiple channels including sites, emails, and apps?
options: Salesforce Knowledge
Salesforce CMS (Content Management System)
Chatter Groups
Document Generation with Experience Cloud
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce CMS is a headless content management system that enables content teams to create and publish structured content (news articles, product descriptions, banners) and deliver it to Experience Cloud sites, Marketing Cloud, and external channels via APIs.
whyWrong: Salesforce Knowledge manages articles but isn't the cross-channel structured content management system being described.
Chatter Groups are for collaboration, not structured multi-channel content publishing.
Document Generation creates documents — it isn't the structured content management system across channels being described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Experience Builder Workspaces in Experience Cloud?
options: The admin panel used to configure, publish, and manage Experience Cloud sites from a central location in Setup
A collaborative space where external users can work together on shared documents
A reporting dashboard that shows site traffic and member engagement metrics
A sandboxed environment for testing Experience Cloud customisations before publishing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workspaces is the central administration area for Experience Cloud sites — accessible from Setup. It contains Experience Builder (visual page editor), Administration (members, login, security), Moderation, Analytics, and Content management panels.
whyWrong: A collaborative document workspace is a different concept, not what Experience Builder Workspaces provides.
A reporting dashboard for traffic is a separate analytics feature, not what Experience Builder Workspaces provides.
A sandboxed testing environment is a different concept from the central admin management panel being described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Lightning Bolt Solution in Experience Cloud?
options: A pre-built, packaged Experience Cloud site template with pages, themes, and components that can be installed from AppExchange and customised
A Lightning Component that adds a live chat widget to an Experience Cloud site
A Salesforce-managed integration that connects Experience Cloud with Slack channels
A mobile app accelerator for generating native iOS and Android apps from a site
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lightning Bolt Solutions are pre-built site packages on AppExchange created by Salesforce ISV partners. They bundle a complete site template — including pages, themes, flows, and custom components — that can be installed and configured for rapid deployment.
whyWrong: A Lightning Component adding chat is a specific component, not the broader packaged site template concept.
A Slack integration is unrelated to Lightning Bolt Solutions, which are AppExchange site templates.
A native mobile app accelerator is a different AppExchange offering, not what a Lightning Bolt Solution is.

sampleQuestions.question: How are Guest User permissions managed in Experience Cloud?
options: Guest users share the same profile as authenticated external users
A dedicated Guest User profile controls what unauthenticated visitors can see and do — including object permissions, field visibility, and record access via guest user sharing rules
Guest users are automatically assigned the Minimum Access - Salesforce profile
Guest user access is managed exclusively through Experience Cloud Workspaces settings
sampleQuestions.explanation: Each Experience Cloud site has a dedicated Guest User profile. Admins control which objects guest users can read, which fields are visible, and which records they can access via guest user sharing rules. Salesforce has tightened guest user security in recent releases — the exam tests which access types require authentication.
whyWrong: Guest users don't share the same profile as authenticated users — they have a distinct Guest User profile.
Guest users aren't automatically assigned 'Minimum Access - Salesforce' — they have a dedicated, sitespecific profile.
Guest user access isn't managed exclusively through Workspaces settings — it's controlled via the dedicated Guest User profile and sharing rules.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature in Experience Cloud allows site admins to show different content to logged-in members vs. unauthenticated guest visitors?
options: Record Detail Page Layouts
Audience-Based Visibility rules applied to components or pages
Profile-Based Page Assignments
Site.com Studio Component Visibility
sampleQuestions.explanation: Audience-Based Visibility in Experience Builder allows admins to define when a component or page is visible — such as showing a login prompt to guests and a personalised dashboard to authenticated members. Audiences can be based on login status, user attributes, or record data.
whyWrong: Record Detail Page Layouts control field display on records, not member-vs-guest content differentiation.
Profile-Based Page Assignments aren't the Experience Cloud-specific mechanism for this — that's Audience-Based Visibility.
Site.com Studio is a legacy tool, not the current Experience Cloud mechanism for audience-based content visibility.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to allow its reseller partners to update shared Opportunity records directly from an Experience Cloud partner portal. What configuration is required?
options: Give partners full Salesforce CRM licences to access the standard Sales Console
Assign partners a Partner Community licence and configure sharing rules or an External Account Hierarchy to grant access to the relevant Opportunity records
Install a custom Apex trigger to sync opportunity updates from the portal to the internal org
Enable the Opportunity object for guest user access in the site settings
sampleQuestions.explanation: Partner Community licences enable external partner users to access Salesforce objects including Opportunities. Sharing must be configured — via sharing rules, sharing sets, or External Account Hierarchy — to grant access to the specific records. Guest user access cannot be used for write operations on CRM records.
whyWrong: Giving partners full internal CRM licenses is costly and unnecessary — Partner Community licenses are the purpose-built solution.
A custom Apex trigger for syncing is unnecessary — native sharing configuration already provides this access.
Enabling guest user access would expose Opportunity data to unauthenticated visitors, which is inappropriate for this scenario.

sampleQuestions.question: Which reporting feature in Experience Cloud allows site members to view reports and dashboards based on their own data?
options: Einstein Analytics embedded in the site via CRM Analytics iFrame
Reports and Dashboards made accessible to external users via sharing settings and the Reports tab in the site
Chatter Feed analytics showing individual post engagement
Salesforce CMS publishing metrics in the content management panel
sampleQuestions.explanation: Standard Salesforce Reports and Dashboards can be made accessible in Experience Cloud sites by adding the Reports tab and configuring sharing so external users see only their own data. For more advanced analytics, CRM Analytics can be embedded within site pages.
whyWrong: CRM Analytics iFrame embedding is a different, more advanced analytics integration, not the standard external Reports/Dashboards access being described.
Chatter Feed analytics tracks post engagement, not general business reporting.
Salesforce CMS publishing metrics track content performance, not general business reports/dashboards.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Sharing Sets in Experience Cloud?
options: To share dashboards only
To grant external users access to records based on their associated Account or Contact
To share files with internal users
To configure site branding
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing Sets grant record access to external users based on the Account or Contact linked to their community user record.
whyWrong: Sharing Sets aren't about dashboards specifically — that's a different reporting concern.
Sharing Sets aren't about internal file sharing — they're specifically for external user record access.
Sharing Sets aren't about site branding — that's a different, unrelated configuration area.
